title: Diagnostic Identification Tests (1°, 2°, 3° Amines)
topics: 4. Discrimination Matrix for Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Amines
4.1 Hinsberg Test (Benzenesulfonyl chloride, Ph-SO₂Cl + NaOH): 1° Soluble, 2° Insoluble, 3° No Reaction
4.2 Carbylamine Test (CHCl₃ + alc. KOH, Δ): Diagnostic Foul-Smelling Isocyanide (R-NC) for 1° Amines Only (Electrophile: :CCl₂)
4.3 Nitrous Acid Test (HNO₂ at 0–5°C): 1° Aliphatic ──► N₂ ↑ + Alcohols; 2° ──► Yellow Oily N-Nitrosamine; 3° ──► Nitrite Salt
Liebermann Nitroso Reaction for Secondary Amines
quickSummary: Hinsberg test (Ph-SO₂Cl): 1° sulfonamide is SOLUBLE in NaOH; 2° sulfonamide is INSOLUBLE in NaOH; 3° does not react. Carbylamine test (CHCl₃ + KOH) yields foul-smelling isocyanides (R-NC) for 1° amines only (electrophile: :CCl₂). Nitrous acid (HNO₂) releases N₂ gas from 1° aliphatic amines and forms yellow oily N-nitrosamines from 2° amines.
summary: Master diagnostic identification tests and separation protocols for primary, secondary, and tertiary amines.

summaryBox.title: Discrimination Rules
summaryBox.takeaway: Hinsberg: 1° = Soluble in NaOH; 2° = Insoluble in NaOH; 3° = No reaction. Carbylamine: 1° only = Foul isocyanide (R-NC). HNO₂: 1° = N₂ ↑; 2° = Yellow oily nitrosamine.

conceptBreakdown.content:
- **Hinsberg Test**: $1^\circ$ amine forms $N$-alkylbenzenesulfonamide with an acidic $	ext{N-H}$ (soluble in $	ext{NaOH}$); $2^\circ$ amine forms $N,N$-dialkylbenzenesulfonamide lacking $	ext{N-H}$ (insoluble in $	ext{NaOH}$); $3^\circ$ amine does not react.
- **Carbylamine Test**: Heated with $	ext{CHCl}_3$ and alcoholic $	ext{KOH}$, $1^\circ$ aliphatic and aromatic amines form intensely foul-smelling isocyanides ($R	ext{-NC}$). Electrophile is Dichlorocarbene ($:	ext{CCl}_2$).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.3 Nitrous Acid Test (0–5°C)
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.3 Nitrous Acid Test (0–5°C)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
NITROUS ACID (HNO₂ = NaNO₂ + HCl at 0–5°C) BEHAVIOR:

• 1° Aliphatic Amine: R-NH₂ + HNO₂ ──► [R-N₂⁺Cl⁻] ──► N₂ ↑ + Mixture of Alcohols/Alkenes
• 1° Aromatic Amine:  Ph-NH₂ + HNO₂ ──► Ph-N₂⁺Cl⁻ (Stable Arenediazonium Salt at 0–5°C)
• 2° Amine:           R₂NH + HNO₂  ──► R₂N-N=O (Yellow Oily Insoluble N-Nitrosamine)
• 3° Amine:           R₃N + HNO₂   ──► R₃NH⁺ NO₂⁻ (Water-Soluble Nitrite Salt)
conceptBreakdown.content: Reaction with $	ext{HNO}_2$ at $0	ext{--}5^\circ	ext{C}$ gives distinct diagnostic outputs for $1^\circ, 2^\circ, 3^\circ$ amines and distinguishes aliphatic from aromatic $1^\circ$ amines.

quickRevision: Hinsberg: 1° = soluble in NaOH; 2° = insoluble in NaOH; 3° = no reaction.
Carbylamine test is positive ONLY for 1° amines (foul R-NC).
Active electrophile in carbylamine test is :CCl₂ (dichlorocarbene).
1° aliphatic amines release N₂ gas with HNO₂.
2° amines form yellow oily N-nitrosamines with HNO₂.
